page: Amazon Web Services c8id.96xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 384 vCPUs across 192 dedicated physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running up to 3.9 GHz. The compute subsystem is equipped with 480 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 768 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. Hardware integration includes 22,800 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 100 Gbps baseline network link, with no discrete GPUs attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests (414,967.5) and PassMark CPU metrics (177,793.0), as well as leading scores in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Large-block memory read bandwidth surpasses 1,148 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput multi-threaded decompression exceeding 1,820 GB/sec. Database and in-memory caching operations are strong, with Redis SET throughput reaching 479.57 million operations per second and static web serving measuring 190.05 GB/sec. While LLM prompt ingestion achieves solid rates using AMX matrix acceleration, autoregressive text generation throughput drops significantly without dedicated GPU accelerators.

The massive core count, dense local NVMe array, and 100 Gbps networking deliver substantial resource density for parallel compute tasks. This balance eliminates external network storage bottlenecks for heavy disk-bound operations. However, workloads requiring high per-thread single-core speeds or large memory-to-vCPU footprints may encounter diminishing returns on this architecture. The instance is suited for large-scale distributed databases, high-throughput caching tiers, parallel code compilation pipelines, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.
